chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him, or a man asked him, about a man whose wife claimed against him that he was impotent, while the man denied that. He said:

The midwife should apply khaluq to her without the man knowing, and he should enter upon her. Then if he comes out and khaluq is on his private part, he has spoken the truth and she has lied; otherwise, she has spoken the truth and he has lied.

key_terms.الْخَلُوقِ: a scented substance used here as a means of verification
key_terms.الْقَابِلَةُ: the midwife who assists in carrying out the test
key_terms.عِنِّينٌ: an impotent man, unable to consummate intercourse

ai.seo_question: How does Shia fiqh verify a claim that a husband is impotent when he denies it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a judicial method for verifying a wife's claim that her husband is impotent when he denies it. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام describes a practical test using khaluq to establish the truth of the claim. The report belongs to family law and legal adjudication in marital disputes.
